chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Kahili, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A house shared by a group, they divided it; each one took a portion, built upon it, and left a courtyard between them for their passage. Then a man came and bought the share of one of them. Is that for him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, but he must close his door and open a door to the road, or descend from the top of the house and close his door. If the owner of the pathway wishes to sell it, then they are more entitled to it; otherwise, it is his pathway, and he comes until he sits at that door.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on pre-emption when a new owner buys a share in a shared house with a common courtyard?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanics of pre-emption (shuf'ah) in shared properties, specifically addressing the rights of co-owners when a new party acquires a share. It establishes that while the new owner may use the shared space, the original co-owners hold the primary right to buy out the new share to preserve their exclusive control over the passage, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preventing harm (darar) and maintaining communal harmony in shared assets.
